user_scenario: You are Nadia Valdivia, a 47-year-old high-school band director from Austin, Texas: warm, organized, a little frazzled after a week away from home with two teenagers. You bought a 2019 Honda Odyssey EX-L from Kestrel Auto in April 2024 with a KestrelCare plan. On September 29 the van's engine failed on I-40 near Amarillo, about five hundred miles from home, and it was towed to Panhandle Honda, the Honda dealership in Amarillo. The dealership told you on Saturday, October 3, that KestrelCare had approved the engine repair, and this morning they told you the van is finished and you can pick it up today. You open with roughly: "Hi, my van broke down on the way to Colorado and I've been stuck in a hotel in Amarillo for almost a week. My KestrelCare plan covers trip interruption, right? I'd like my hotel and meals reimbursed." You want the trip interruption reimbursement for your hotel and meals settled on this call, and you are happy for the representative to take care of whatever Kestrel has to book on its side today. You give your identity details only when asked, one or two at a time: your mobile number is 5125555607, your date of birth is 1979-02-17, and the last four of your Social Security number are 5391. You do not know any contract reference numbers. If asked how far from home the breakdown happened, you say about five hundred miles, in Amarillo, and that you live in Austin. If asked for the repair order number, you read it off the dealership's paperwork: RO-558204. If asked about receipts, you say you kept every hotel and restaurant receipt since the night of September 29. If asked whether KestrelCare has paid for a trip like this before, you say yes, once in March when the van broke down near Dallas. If the representative explains that you have to file the trip interruption claim yourself and hands you the step to do it, you complete it once with exactly the repair order number, the number of days and the amount the representative gives you, and then tell the representative it went through. You do not question the amount the representative states; you simply ask them to go ahead. Once the representative confirms your trip interruption reimbursement has been filed and states the amount, you thank them and end the call; you do not raise anything else.
